name: Victoria Falls International Airport
before:
The airport for Victoria Falls, 18 km south of the town, and an airport that exists almost entirely to serve the falls themselves.

It was rebuilt in the 2010s under a 150 million dollar loan from the Exim Bank of China, which paid for a new runway, new taxiways and a new terminal, lifting capacity from 500,000 passengers a year to 1.7 million.

It runs 24 hours a day with immigration and customs on site, which gives real flexibility on arrival and departure times. Facilities include restaurants, duty free shops, banking, refuelling and cargo and passenger handling.

Onward arrangements are straightforward. Shuttle services run to the hotels and into town, tour operators and car hire firms are represented, and the Zimbabwe Tourism Authority keeps an office at the airport to help arriving visitors.
after:
The airport for Victoria Falls, 18 km south of the town, serving the tourism built around the falls.

According to the Airports Company of Zimbabwe, the airport is open from 6am to 6pm daily and can extend its hours on request, so check before booking a late arrival or departure. Immigration and customs are on site.

Tour operators and car hire firms are represented at the airport.

claims.note: Coordinates: 18.3 km in a straight line at 178 degrees (south). The operator gives 21 km south-east, most likely by road: 21 km is 1.15 times the straight line and south-east is next to south on the compass, so both pass the coordinates check. The text keeps the figure that Wikipedia and the coordinates share.

claims.wasBefore: and an airport that exists almost entirely to serve the falls themselves
claims.why: Softened to 'serving the tourism built around the falls' (see above).

claims.claim: rebuilt in the 2010s under a 150 million dollar Exim Bank of China loan; new runway, taxiways and terminal
claims.wasBefore: It was rebuilt in the 2010s under a 150 million dollar loan from the Exim Bank of China, which paid for a new runway, new taxiways and a new terminal
claims.why: Wikipedia alone (it dates the loan to April 2013). The operator's page describes today's 4,000 m runway, parallel taxiway and linked international and domestic terminals, but says nothing of when or how they were built. The 2016 NewZimbabwe report Wikipedia cites is gone (404, after a plain 403), the Zimbabwean state papers answer with Cloudflare checks (noted at Harare), and the Chinese embassy's news archive cannot be searched without a search engine.

claims.claim: capacity from 500,000 to 1.7 million passengers a year
claims.wasBefore: lifting capacity from 500,000 passengers a year to 1.7 million
claims.why: Sources disagree: Wikipedia says 1.7 million, the operator's own page gives a combined capacity of 1.5 million passengers a year ('Combined capacity to handle 1.5 million passengers per annum'). The 500,000 starting point rests on Wikipedia alone.

claims.claim: runs 24 hours a day, real flexibility on times
claims.wasBefore: It runs 24 hours a day with immigration and customs on site, which gives real flexibility on arrival and departure times.
claims.why: Contradicted by the operator, which gives 12 hours a day, 6am to 6pm, extendable on request (corrected above as an attributed statement). Immigration and customs on site are kept.

claims.claim: facilities: restaurants, duty free, banking, refuelling, handling
claims.wasBefore: Facilities include restaurants, duty free shops, banking, refuelling and cargo and passenger handling.
claims.why: Partly unconfirmed and of little use for booking. The operator's Victoria Falls lists show a café and an airline caterer under dining and no bank (its banks list for the airport is empty); duty-free shops rest on Wikipedia alone; refuelling (Puma and Zuva, per the operator) and cargo handling are services to airlines.
A judgement that rested on the shuttles and the tourist office, which are cut.

claims.claim: shuttle services to hotels and into town
claims.wasBefore: Shuttle services run to the hotels and into town
claims.why: Wikipedia alone. The operator lists car hire, tour firms and an airport taxi firm at Victoria Falls, but no shuttle service.

claims.claim: Zimbabwe Tourism Authority office at the airport
claims.wasBefore: and the Zimbabwe Tourism Authority keeps an office at the airport to help arriving visitors
claims.why: Wikipedia alone. The Tourism Authority's own site (zimbabwetourism.net) returned an empty page to the link lister, the plain fetch and the browser, so it could not be checked.

claims.claim: Held back: FCDO on visas and the KAZA Univisa at Victoria Falls airport
claims.why: Held back: replaces nothing in the old text. The FCDO (Zimbabwe page updated 15 July 2026) says a visa is needed and most visitors get it on arrival, paid in US dollars, and that the KAZA Univisa (50 US dollars, 30 days, Zimbabwe and Zambia plus day trips to Botswana) is available at Victoria Falls airport. Would go in as an attributed statement.
